summary: Decoder-first RE of the Wiz6 maze wall-texture pipeline. (A) IN-RAM FORMAT — CONFIRMED + VISUALLY DEMONSTRATED: the cell format is 8x8-pixel, 4-plane EGA, 32 bytes/cell; plane p occupies cell bytes [p*8 .. p*8+7] (one byte = one 8-px row of that plane), pixel(r,c) = bit(7-c) of each plane row, color = p0 | p1<<1 | p2<<2 | p3<<3, color 15 (all planes set) = transparent. This is the SAME cell format as the already-SOLVED .pic monster sprites (docs/re/pic.md, packages/parser/src/formats/pic.ts, byte-perfect vs engine). I re-derived it from ega.drv FUN_210c's full Ghidra decompile AND validated it end-to-end by decoding mon11.pic offline into a clean, recognizable armored-warrior sprite (/tmp/mon11_sprite.png). (B/C) ON-DISK mazedata.ega: it is NOT a single RLE stream like .pic (the header byte 0x99 would be a bogus RLE run; whole-file RLE dies after 693 bytes). Structure = 8-byte header + 153x5-byte RAW descriptor table (byte 8) + a second table (byte 0x305, count 366 from header) + a compressed/encoded graphics blob. The descriptor table parses cleanly: {u8 type, u16LE graphic_offset, u8 w, u8 h}. EGA<->CGA comparison nails the semantics: type is identical EGA==CGA (a logical category/ID); graphic_offset is EGA = exactly 2x CGA (a byte offset into the graphics blob; EGA graphics cost 2x bytes); w is EGA = 2x CGA (width in BYTES — scales with plane count: EGA 4 planes vs CGA 2); h is identical (height in rows/px). The graphics blob is NOT raw 4-plane-at-offset (tested -> noise) and tile gaps != w*h, with w=0 entries still consuming bytes -> the blob uses a variable-length (likely RLE/masked) encoding whose exact algorithm + the second table's role (banks? mask/script?) remain UNRESOLVED — they require a live trace of the mazedata graphics decode, which is the genuine 'deeper RE problem' the prior commits flagged. The 0x57/0x33/0x1b/0x70 'depth-face cycle' hypothesis is WRONG as a global pattern: it only holds for the first ~11 descriptors and is coincidental; the type byte ranges 0x02..0x70+ with histogram dominated by 0x10(29x).

findings.claim: RESOLVED — THE 'DECOMPRESSOR' IS THE .pic RLE DECODER, RUN FROM A RELOCATED COPY. The maze graphics are decompressed by the SAME byte-for-byte RLE decoder documented in docs/re/pic.md (ega.drv dispatch entry 9 @ file 0x1c25), NOT a bespoke format. The engine COPIES that decoder into a transient work-buffer and EXECUTES it there (live cs:ip 0x6d635 in the captured session) — which is exactly why every prior static breakpoint on the in-image ega.drv:0x1c25 logged 0 hits (the in-image copy is never executed during graphics load). The relocated decoder body is BYTE-IDENTICAL to ega.drv[0x1c6c..0x1c8c]. Algorithm (identical to pic.md): lseek SEEK_SET to a file offset, read 4096-byte chunks into a DOS read buffer (live seg 0x6a0f), then RLE-decode: op==0 END; op<0x80 LIT(op) rep-movsb; op>=0x80 RUN(256-op) of next byte rep-stosb; the byte at buffer offset 0xFFF is dropped on refill (cmp si,0xfff; jae refill). Output goes to ES:DI (the dest segment chosen via cs:[0x17a+2*destIdx] + cs:[0x169]). The decoded CELL is the confirmed 4-plane EGA 8x8 32-byte cell. So the 'mazedata graphics blob is a custom RLE/mask encoding' hypothesis from the prior pass is WITHDRAWN — the pixel tiles are produced by the standard .pic decoder.

evidence.details: Captured the transient decoder code at live lin 0x6d600 (capture-on-breakpoint armed on cseip 0x6d698, the RUN rep-stosb). Capstone of 0x6d635..0x6d6a3: `push bp; mov bp,sp; sub sp,8; ...; mov ax,[bp+0x16]; shl ax,1; mov bx,0x17a; add bx,ax; mov ax,cs:[bx]; mov bx,cs:[0x169]; add bx,ax; mov es,bx; mov ds,cs:[0x16d]; mov ah,0x42; mov al,0; mov bx,[bp+0xc]; mov cx,[bp+0x10]; mov dx,[bp+0xe]; int 0x21; xor di,di; <refill> mov cx,0x1000; mov ah,0x3f; int 0x21; xor si,si; <loop> cmp si,0xfff; jae refill; lodsb; or al,al; je end; test al,0x80; jne run; mov cl,al; rep movsb; jmp loop; <run> neg al; mov cl,al; lodsb; rep stosb; jmp loop; <end> pop di/si/es/ds; mov sp,bp; pop bp; ret`. Byte-compare: relocated [0x6d67c..0x6d6a4] == ega.drv[0x1c6c..0x1c8c] EXACTLY (`81 fe ff 0f 73 ec 33 c9 ac 0a c0 74 13 a8 80 75 06 8a c8 f3 a4 eb e9 f6 d8 8a c8 ac f3 aa eb e0 5f 5e 07 1f 8b e5 5d c3`). Live trace of the lseek (cseip 0x6d66a) across boot: 10 whole-file decodes, all SEEK_SET offset 0, dest segs {0x4e0e,0x4f8e,0x514e,0x540e,0x550e,0x670e,0x680e,0x690e}. The dispatch-9 in-image trace at boot+title logged 0 hits (consistent — the executed copy is the transient one).

findings.claim: WORKED VALIDATION — the wall tile atlas decodes to clean grey stone (NOT noise) when read at LOAD time. The corridor wall blit (live cseip ega_base+0x3a25 == 0x6dbd5) reads its source from seg 0x550e (and 0x514e), active si window from 0x2138. Decoding the 8-cell column the blit actually reads (si=0x2138, +0x20/cell) from a CAPTURE-AT-LOAD snapshot of seg 0x550e gives a coherent dithered texture: color histogram {8 (dark grey):269, 13 (light, EGA-default magenta -> grey under Wiz6 palette overrides):129, 0 (black, mortar):114} and NOTHING else. The earlier 'decodes to noise' result is explained: a SETTLED-FRAME read() of seg 0x550e returns STALE/OVERWRITTEN bytes (the buffer is reused after the load compose). You MUST capture seg 0x550e with the capture-on-breakpoint tool armed on the blit during the LOAD compose to read the real atlas. The 4-plane cell formula (G=byte[0..7], B=[8..15], R=[16..23], I=[24..31], color=G|B<<1|R<<2|I<<3, 15=transparent) decodes it correctly — example cell @si=0x2138 bytes `00002204922448920000000000000000 00002204922448920 0aa77aeff7eedff` has plane1 (B)=all-zero and plane0(G)==plane2(R), yielding only colors 0/8/13 — a stone dither.

evidence.details: trace-blit-src (same session): blit at 0x6dbd5 reads ds=0x550e si 0x2138,0x2139..0x213f then 0x2158 (+0x20); also ds=0x514e. Captured seg 0x550e0 (0x4000 bytes) on the first blit hit during the dungeon LOAD compose (-> /tmp/mazere/atlas-load-550e.bin). Offline 4-plane decode of the 8 cells at 0x2138 step 0x20: histogram {8:269,13:129,0:114}; rendered /tmp/mazere/wall-col.png = dithered grey/magenta stone (magenta = unremapped EGA-13). A settled-frame read() of the same seg returns different (stale) bytes that decode to noise — the prior pass's source-region-decode-not-stone result was reading stale data, not a wrong format.

findings.claim: mazedata.ega is the maze INDEX/DESCRIPTOR file (NOT the wall pixel source). It is loaded into RAM ESSENTIALLY VERBATIM (in the captured runs at lin 0x1ffb0 = seg 0x1ffb): the graphics blob region (file 0x305..end) is BYTE-IDENTICAL disk<->RAM (0 diffs across ~99700 bytes). Only the 8-byte header and the 153x5-byte descriptor table are transformed IN PLACE at load: (1) header bytes 4..5 (a u16, 0 on disk) are REWRITTEN to 0x00A2 and byte 6 (0 on disk) to 0x07 — the 0xA2 is the base descriptor-relocation delta; (2) each descriptor's goff (u16LE) += base delta 0xA2, EXCEPT w==12 entries get +0xA3 (a +1 alignment bump) and the single w==40 entry is unchanged (delta 0); (3) each descriptor's w byte is replaced by a 4-bit EGA column edge-mask {disk w=0->0x07, 4->0x0b, 8->0x0f, 12->0x03; w=40 stays 40}, depending ONLY on disk w; (4) type and h are unchanged. tools/parity/decode-mazedata.ts reproduces the relocated table BYTE-EXACTLY (0/153 goff mismatches, 0/153 w mismatches vs the live RAM dump). The prior pass's claim that the descriptor table 'is not kept verbatim in RAM' is correct only in the narrow sense that goff/w are rewritten; the file is otherwise contiguous in RAM.

evidence.details: Same-session: blob sig (disk bytes at 0xa2b: ff17ff7f87fc9e17f7787ddb7bc3db1f) found in RAM at 0x209db -> header = 0x209db-0xa2b = 0x1ffb0; full 102303-byte image dumped (/tmp/mazere/mazedata-ram2.bin). Diff vs disk: 0 diffs at/after 0x305; 397 diffs all within bytes 4..0x2fe (header reloc-word + descriptor goff/w). RAM header = `99 00 6e 01 a2 00 07 0e` (disk `99 00 6e 01 00 00 00 0e`). RAM desc[0] = `57 d2 01 0f 08` (disk `57 30 01 08 08`): goff 0x130->0x1d2 (+0xA2), w 8->0x0f mask, h 8 unchanged. goff-delta histogram over all 153: {0xA2:117, 0xA3:35 (all w=12), 0:1 (the w=40 entry)}; w-transform is the 5-value map above. decode-mazedata.ts (relocateDescriptors) reproduces this BYTE-EXACTLY: 0/153 goff mismatches, 0/153 w mismatches vs /tmp/mazere/mazedata-ram2.bin.

findings.claim: The in-RAM maze/sprite texture CELL is 8x8 px, 4-plane EGA, 32 bytes. Layout: cell byte [p*8 + r] = plane p (p in 0..3), row r (r in 0..7), MSB = leftmost pixel. color(r,c) = (G[r]>>(7-c)&1) | (B[r]>>(7-c)&1)<<1 | (R[r]>>(7-c)&1)<<2 | (I[r]>>(7-c)&1)<<3, where G=bytes0..7, B=8..15, R=16..23, I=24..31. Color 15 (all 4 planes set at a pixel) = TRANSPARENT. This is IDENTICAL to the already-solved .pic cell format (docs/re/pic.md lines 60-86). The masked merge in ega.drv is dst = src&~transp | dst&transp where transp = p0&p1&p2&p3 per byte.

evidence.details: Ghidra decompile of FUN_210c (ega.drv 0x210c, dispatch entry 10) inner loop: `iVar5=8; do { bVar7 = src[0]&src[8]&src[0x10]&src[0x18]; bVar8=~bVar7; dst[0]=src[0]&bVar8|dst[0]&bVar7; dst[8]=...; dst[0x10]=...; dst[0x18]=...; src+=1; dst+=1; } while(--iVar5); src+=0x19; dst+=0x19` (per cell: src/dst advance 0x20 total = 4 planes x 8 bytes). Descriptor walk: puVar3=(in_AL-1)*0x18 (1-indexed, stride 0x18), pbVar11=*puVar3 (source pixel ptr), (BP-2)=width-in-cells, (BP-4)=height-in-rows, puVar3+2=presence bitmap. VALIDATION: decoded mon11.pic offline with this exact cell formula (after the pic.md RLE step) -> /tmp/mon11_sprite.png renders a clean armored warrior with a blue sword (W=9 H=13 cells). The formula is byte-exact (pic.ts already passes byte-perfect parity vs the engine per pic.md).

findings.claim: The live corridor WALL compose blit (the load-time texture compositor, cseip lin 0x6dbd5 .. 0x6dc07 = 4 plane stores) uses the SAME masked 4-plane merge as FUN_210c. Per cell: read source ds:si planes at si+0/+8/+0x10/+0x18, AND for transparency, merge into es:di compose page, inner cx=8 (8 px-byte positions), then si+=0x18/di+=0x18 (so +0x20 per cell-row). Source and dest cell-starts advance in LOCKSTEP +0x20 contiguously (si 0x2138,0x2158,0x2178,...; di 0x60,0x80,0xa0,...) -> the blit is a 1:1 masked copy of a contiguous source region into a contiguous compose region; the perspective/U-V is entirely in the OUTER driver's choice of which source region maps to which compose region.

evidence.details: trace-maze.ts drvtrace 0x6dbd5 during the dungeon LOAD compose (fresh boot -> 3-member party -> START NEW GAME -> dungeon). Live: ds=0x550e (source seg), es=0x6a0f (compose page). Cell-start trace (cx=8): si=0x2138 di=0x60; si=0x2158 di=0x80; si=0x2178 di=0xa0; ... (both +0x20/cell, contiguous). ax = the source texel byte being merged. findings.claim: mazedata.ega is one of winit.ovr's init-time asset loads (filename 'MAZEDATA.EGA' at winit.ovr file 0x12a9, in the .EGA/.CGA/.T16 video-mode filename table 0x1272..0x1331). It is NOT loaded via the .pic RLE decoder (ega.drv 0x1c25, dispatch entry 9) — that decoder logs 0 hits across boot+title. The file is also TRANSFORMED at load: neither its header (99 00 6e 01) nor its descriptor-table signature (57 30 01 08 08) appears verbatim anywhere in live RAM at the corridor frame. So a load-time decode/restructure happens (the descriptor table is not kept verbatim, or graphics are decompressed into a separate heap).

evidence.details: strings -t x winit.ovr: 0x12a9 'MAZEDATA.EGA' (alongside WFONT0-4.EGA at 0x1272-0x129e). Live: trace ega.drv+0x1c25 (RLE decoder entry 9) across boot+title = 0 hits. Live find('99006e0100') and find('5730010808339601') in the corridor frame = NOT FOUND. The .pic family RLE decode of the WHOLE mazedata.ega dies after 693 bytes (0x99 -> bogus RUN of 0x00), so it is not a single RLE stream from byte 0.

findings.claim: mazedata.ega on-disk layout: bytes 0..7 = header (u16 153 = descriptor count; u16 366 = second-table count; u16 0; bytes 0x00 0x0e). Bytes 8..0x304 (765 B) = Table 1: 153 x 5-byte descriptors, struct { u8 type, u16LE graphic_offset, u8 w, u8 h }. desc[0] = {type=0x57, goff=0x130, w=8, h=8}. Bytes 0x305.. = Table 2 (count 366, record size/role TBD — recurring 0x34 0x00 / 0x3c 0x00 / 0x28 0x00 word patterns). Graphics blob follows. The descriptor table is stored RAW (the first 8 bytes + the type/h fields are byte-identical between mazedata.ega and mazedata.cga).

evidence.details: Header hex 99 00 6e 01 00 00 00 0e. Descriptor pattern 57 30 01 08 08 found at file 0x8 (5-byte stride parses 153 entries cleanly: desc0 type=57 goff=304 w8 h8; desc1 33 406 8 4; desc2 1b 433 8 4; desc3 70 545 8 3; ...). Table ends at 0x305 (=8+153*5). Table2 dump at 0x305: 0e 01 10 34 00 | 08 02 12 3c 00 | 04 00 00 08 00 ... EGA vs CGA: headers identical; per-descriptor type & h identical, goff & w halve in CGA.

findings.claim: Descriptor field semantics, pinned by the EGA<->CGA diff: (1) type (u8) is a logical category/ID (identical EGA==CGA for every descriptor). (2) graphic_offset (u16LE) is a BYTE OFFSET into the graphics blob; EGA value = exactly 2x CGA value for every descriptor (EGA graphics cost 2x bytes b/c 4 planes vs CGA 2). (3) w (u8) is WIDTH IN BYTES of the graphic (EGA = exactly 2x CGA — scales with plane count), NOT cells; for an 8x8 tile EGA stores w=8. (4) h (u8) is HEIGHT in rows/px (identical EGA==CGA). The 0x57/0x33/0x1b/0x70 'depth-face' cycle is NOT a global pattern — it holds only for the first ~11 descriptors; type ranges 0x02..0x70+ across all 153 (histogram dominated by 0x10 x29).

evidence.details: Per-descriptor EGA/CGA: desc0 type 57==57, goff 304/152 (2.00x), w 8/4 (2x), h 8==8. desc1 33==33, 406/203, 8/4, 4==4. desc2 1b==1b, 433/216, w 8/12(!), 4==4. desc4 57==57, 610/305, 12/6, 2==2. goff ratio is a clean 2.00x throughout; w ratio is 2x where comparable; h always identical. type histogram over 153: {0x10:29, 0x57:8, 0x05:8, 0x1c:8, 0x70:6, 0x33:7, 0x58:7, ...} — not a 4-value cycle.

findings.claim: SUPERSEDED by decompressor-is-pic-rle-decoder-relocated + wall-atlas-renders-grey-stone-load-capture. (Original OPEN note retained for history.) The reason 'raw 4-plane at goff' decoded to noise: (a) the wall PIXEL atlas the blit reads is in a SEPARATE .pic-RLE-decoded segment (live 0x550e/0x514e), not at (mazedata_blob + goff); mazedata.ega's blob is the index file's payload, addressed by the relocated goff but consumed by the .pic decoder / further composition, not as a flat 32-byte cell grid at goff; (b) every offline decode read STALE settled-frame bytes — the load-time capture decodes to clean grey stone. ORIGINAL CLAIM: the graphics blob is NOT raw 4-plane tiles addressed by graphic_offset. Decoding desc[0..N] at (graphics_base + goff) as raw 32-byte 4-plane 8x8 cells (multiple graphics_base candidates: 0, 0x305, 0x5e1, 0xA2B) all yield colored NOISE, never grey stone. Tile gaps (goff[k+1]-goff[k]) do NOT equal w*h for 146/152 descriptors, and w=0 descriptors still consume blob bytes -> the blob uses a VARIABLE-LENGTH (likely RLE / mask-packed) encoding where w/h are DECODED dimensions, not encoded size. The gaps DO scale exactly 2x EGA-vs-CGA, so the encoding is plane-count-linear (raw-ish per-plane), not entropy-compressed (file entropy is low, 3-5 bits, 42-66% zero — consistent with sparse planar/masked, not Huffman). The exact decode (RLE? mask+run like .pic but with the mask in Table 2? per-bank windowing via the 366-entry table?) is UNRESOLVED and needs a live trace of the mazedata graphics decode path.

evidence.details: Rendered desc[0..30] as raw 4-plane (w*h cells, 32B each) at graphics_base in {0,0x305,0x5e1,0xA2B} -> /tmp/ega_gb*.png, all colored noise. gap==w*h only 6/152 times. Per-4KB entropy 3.30-6.06 bits, zero-fraction 0.42-0.66. Whole-file RLE (pic.md algorithm) terminates after 693 B. RLE from candidate graphics starts (0x305/0x5e1/0xA2B) terminates after 14/40/402 B -> no clean single RLE stream there either.

The 4-plane cell format (egadrv-blit-internals.json) stands and is now also confirmed by the grey-stone load-capture decode.
